rule: A local butcher comes first; at the case, choose meat from animals raised on grass and open pasture.
checks: Ask what the animal ate and how it lived; a butcher counter can answer.
Organs come from the same animal; liver and heart belong in the cart too.
On packaged meat, look for an ingredient list of meat, salt, and spices.
beyond: Better than any case: a butcher, or a farm that sells its meat direct.

rule: Eggs and dairy start with how the animal ate and lived: cows on grass, hens on pasture.
checks: Read how the animal lived and what it ate before anything else on the label.
Dairy needs few ingredients: milk or cream, cultures, salt, and enzymes for cheese.
beyond: Better than any carton: eggs and milk from a farm you can visit.

rule: Choose produce grown organic or unsprayed, and pick it whole and in season.
checks: Local and in season comes first; ask the produce staff what that is this week.
Frozen fruit and vegetables with nothing added count as whole food too.
beyond: Better than any shelf: the farmers market, picked this week.

rule: Wild-caught fish ate its natural diet; choose wild first and ask where it was caught.
checks: Ask the counter where the fish was caught and how.
beyond: Better than any case: a fishmonger who can name the boat.

rule: Choose packages with a short list of real ingredients and only natural fats: tallow, olive oil, coconut oil.
checks: Skip seed oils and avocado oil, whatever the front of the package says.
The ingredient line tells more than the front; read it first.

rule: Frozen food counts as whole when the bag lists the food and nothing else.
checks: Frozen meals follow the pantry rule: real ingredients, natural fats only.
